title: Filtering with Where
description: Learn to filter collections using the Where operator with predicates and lambda expressions.

data.text: Filtering operators in LINQ filter a sequence (collection) based on specified criteria. The most commonly used filtering operator is **Where**.
The `Where` extension method filters a collection based on a given criteria expression and returns a new collection. The criteria can be specified as a lambda expression or `Func` delegate.

data.text: In this example, the lambda expression `s.Age > 12 && s.Age < 20` is passed as a predicate function `Func<Student, bool>` that evaluates every student in the collection.

Key Takeaways
points: Where filters collections based on a predicate function
Two overloads: with and without index parameter
Can use lambda expressions, anonymous methods, or named methods as predicates
Multiple Where clauses can be chained for complex filtering
data.takeaway: Continue to the next lesson to learn about the OfType filtering operator.
